o: Aggregate points per (country, winery), rank wineries within each country by total points descending (ties broken by name ascending), then pivot ranks 1–3 into three columns, substituting placeholder text when a rank is missing. USA illustrates aggregation: RoyalVines totals 47+39=86 across two rows.
k: Group by country and winery first, then rank with a window function.
Pivot with conditional aggregation (MAX CASE) and COALESCE for missing ranks.

a.i: Inner query computes SUM(points) grouped by country/winery and assigns RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY total DESC, winery ASC). Outer query pivots with MAX(CASE WHEN rk=k ...) wrapped in CONCAT for the '(points)' suffix, defaulting to 'No second/third winery' via IFNULL/COALESCE.
s: Group by country, winery; sum points.
Rank within country by points DESC, winery ASC.
Conditionally aggregate ranks 1, 2, 3 into formatted strings.

c.python:
SELECT country,
       IFNULL(CONCAT(MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN winery END), ' (', MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN pts END), ')'), 'No top winery') AS top_winery,
       IFNULL(CONCAT(MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN winery END), ' (', MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN pts END), ')'), 'No second winery') AS second_winery,
       IFNULL(CONCAT(MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 3 THEN winery END), ' (', MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 3 THEN pts END), ')'), 'No third winery') AS third_winery
FROM (
    SELECT country, winery, SUM(points) AS pts,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY SUM(points) DESC, winery ASC) AS rk
    FROM Wineries
    GROUP BY country, winery
) t
GROUP BY country
ORDER BY country;

a.t: O(m log m) for the window sort over m aggregated (country, winery) rows.

w: Common mistakes: aggregating points before deduplicating winery names (RoyalVines appears twice), using ROW_NUMBER vs RANK (tie handling), and forgetting the exact placeholder strings. In PostgreSQL use TO_CHAR or || concatenation and COALESCE instead of IFNULL/CONCAT.
